about.title: About & Privacy
about.whatBody: An AI lab that runs entirely in the browser, letting students train machine-learning models and see every step the AI takes with their data.
privacyItems: Images, sounds and text you add are stored only in this browser on this device (IndexedDB).
The site has no server receiving data, no tracking cookies and no analytics.
Only when you press "Export" does your data become a file on your device. You decide who gets it.
Camera and microphone turn on only with your permission and turn off when you leave the page.
about.sharedBody: Delete your data before leaving so others cannot see your projects.
about.deleteAll: Delete all data on this device
about.confirmDeleteAll: Delete ALL LUP Machine projects in this browser? This cannot be undone.

quality.lead: The assistant reviews the Train data before training.

issues.too-few-classes: You need at least 2 classes for the machine to tell something apart.
issues.empty-class: Class "{{label}}" has no Train images yet.
issues.too-few-samples: Class "{{label}}" has only {{count}} Train images. Aim for at least {{minimum}}.
issues.class-imbalance: Class "{{largest}}" has {{ratio}}× more images than "{{smallest}}". The model may favour the larger class.
issues.no-test-samples: Class "{{label}}" has no Test images, so it cannot be scored.

tips.empty-class: Upload images or capture with the webcam.
tips.too-few-samples: Capture more from different angles and lighting.
tips.class-imbalance: Add images to the smaller class or remove some from the larger one.
tips.no-test-samples: Press "Auto-split" or move a few images to Test.

inspector.title: Microscope · What does the computer see?
inspector.exactHint: These are exactly the numbers the model receives.
inspector.imageLabel: 224 × 224 image. Click or use arrow keys to pick a pixel.
inspector.howBody: When you add an image, the site crops the largest centred square, resizes it to 224 × 224 pixels and stores it. The numbers here are read directly from that stored image, which is exactly what goes into MobileNetV2. Normalisation uses v / 127.5 − 1, identical to the original training of the model.
